title: Sweetwater Grade 1 lesson plan, week of Nov 9
scope: Excerpts only: lesson-content lines ClassThread items cite. No names, rosters, small-group links or student information.
content:
[Foundations 11/9, Monday (session 1), Learning Targets] Blends sounds together to make a word. - Read and write words with cr and fr.
[Foundations 11/9, Tuesday (session 2), Word Bank] Word Bank: frog, crab, crown, first
[Foundations 11/9, Wednesday (session 3), Learning Targets] Blend letters to make a word. - Read and write words with dr and tr.
[Foundations 11/9, Wednesday (session 3), Word Bank] Word Bank: dream, dress, trap, truck
[Foundations 11/9, Thursday (session 4), Word Bank] Word Bank: drink, drip, trace, tray
[Foundations 11/9, Friday (session 5), Retrieval Activator] None-Test Day
[Foundations 11/9, Vocabulary & Strategy] Unit Vocabulary: deep, habitat, ocean, shallow Key Vocabulary: dives, surface, rises, animals, water, kelp, forest, sea, surround, tangle, swells Super Words: into, more, one, your
[Literacy 11/9, Wednesday (Session 3), CER] Claim: The deepest parts of the ocean are dark.
[Literacy 11/9, Friday (Session 5), CER] Evidence: The text says kelp forests provide a home and keep animals safe from other animals and storms.
[Writing 11/9, Tuesday, I Do] Point out the proper noun Pacific Ocean and explain that Pacific Ocean is a proper noun because it names a specific ocean.
[Writing 11/9, Wednesday, I Do] Model writing the sentence and explain that word coast is a place where the water meets the land.
[Writing 11/9, Thursday, I Do] Tell students that today they will facts about habitat. Remind students what habitats are.
[Writing 11/9, Thursday, We Do] Remind students that the subject and verb must sound right together.
[M 11/9, Lesson Title] Unit: 3- Solving Word Problems and Making Comparisons Lesson 11- Solve Word Problems to 20
[M 11/9, Monday - Session 1, Learning Target] Today I will model and solve word problems within 20 using objects, pictures, or numbers.
[Science 11/9, Standard] S1E1.b Ask questions to identify forms of precipitation such as rain, snow, sleet, and hailstones as either solid (ice) or liquid (water).
[Science 11/9, Instructions, Day 1] Ask students what they know about precipitation.
[Science 11/9, Instructions, Day 2] Talk about the difference between a solid and a liquid. Ask students if rain and snow are solids or liquid.
[Science 11/9, Instructions, Day 3] Tell students that today they learn about sleet and hail.
[Science 11/9, CER, Day 3] Day 3 – Sleet and Hail. Question: Is sleet or hail a solid or a liquid?
